rows.title: Implement the interactive Lovelace REPL.
evidence: `rust/target/debug/lovelace-run.exe --repl` with the script `func g(x) { ... } g(2)` piped on stdin: prints `LovelaceSharp REPL v1.0.0`, the two banner lines and blank line, `» ` prompts, `= 3 (Natural)   [164.4 µs]`, then `Bye!`; exit 0, stderr empty
`cargo test -p lovelace-run --test repl` — 11 passed, 0 failed: every transcript test spawns the built binary and compares the whole piped session
`rust/target/debug/lovelace-run.exe --repl --eval 1+1` — exit 2, stderr `error: --repl cannot be combined with a script source or registry query` plus usage
`rust/target/debug/lovelace-run.exe --help` — exit 0 and lists `--repl interactive session (stdin/stdout; Ctrl+C exits)`
rows.note: The REPL exists in rust/lovelace-run (repl.rs, --repl in main.rs). Round 104 drove the built binary through a pipe; the four-line banner, prompts, evaluation, EOF/exit and error paths are exercised.

rows.title: Preserve multiline statement accumulation.
evidence: `lovelace-run --repl` piped `func g(x) {` / `  x + 1` / `}` / `g(2)`: the continuation lines are read under the `… ` prompt and the balanced block is evaluated once, printing `= 3 (Natural)   [164.4 µs]`; exit 0
`cargo test -p lovelace-run --test repl` — multiline_accumulation_runs_the_block_after_braces_balance and continuation_end_of_input_still_prints_bye_once pass (11 passed, 0 failed)
`lovelace-run::repl::tests::braces_must_balance_for_continuation` — the literal `{`/`}` counting rule matches the C# reference (including a negative depth counting as balanced)
rows.note: Accumulation matches ReplSession.cs: the first line is trimmed, continuation lines are appended verbatim, and a balanced brace depth submits the statement.

rows.title: Support editing, history, and keyboard navigation.
evidence: `cargo test -p lovelace-run repl::tests` — 9 passed, including line_buffer_edits_at_the_cursor, history_navigation_restores_the_draft, ansi_navigation_sequences_decode_to_keys, ctrl_c_interrupts_the_line and interactive_editor_submits_edited_and_historical_lines

`interactive_editor_submits_edited_and_historical_lines` drives `read_interactive` with real key bytes: `hi\x1b[D!\r` submits `h!i` (insert at cursor), `\x1b[A\r` recalls it from history, `\x1b[A\x1b[Bx\r` restores the empty draft and submits `x`, `\x03` returns None
ANSI decoding is exercised for Up/Down/Left/Right/Home/End/Delete and UTF-8 input; history is remembered for every non-blank submitted line

Not exercised: the Windows virtual-terminal / Unix `stty` raw-mode handshake that turns real keystrokes into those bytes. `--repl` under a pipe takes the plain path, and a ConPTY harness in this session aborts every child with 0xC0000142 before any byte is exchanged
rows.note: Editing, history and navigation are implemented and unit-tested at the byte-driven editor loop; the gap is the terminal raw-mode layer, which this headless session cannot exercise end-to-end (no console, ConPTY unavailable).

rows.title: Preserve interactive commands and help.

rows.note: The command set, help text and exact messages match the reference console; `run <file>` stream output and the missing-file CLR sentence are transcript-tested.

rows.title: Maintain engine state between commands.

`cargo test -p lovelace-run --test repl` — state_persists_between_commands_and_underscore_tracks_the_last_result and precision_knobs_apply_to_later_commands pass

rows.title: Match precision handling and _ result behavior.

`_` after every successful non-void result: `_ * 3` evaluates to `= 15 (Natural)` and `vars` lists `_ = 16 (Natural)` after `f(4)`
`cargo test -p lovelace-run --test repl` — precision_knobs_apply_to_later_commands and the `_` assertions in state_persists_between_commands_and_underscore_tracks_the_last_result pass

rows.title: Match errors, cancellation, and output formatting.
